triples.evidence: Checks run cheapest first and before the body is read: Host/Origin, bearer, id syntax, known id, Content-Encoding, declared length, concurrency, quota reservation.
Checks run cheapest first and before the body is read: Host/Origin, bearer, id syntax, known id, Content-Encoding, declared length, concurrency, quota reservation.
Every one needs `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and passes the Host/Origin check.
The id is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the decoded bytes, so equal content has one id whatever codec it travelled in.
Upload headers: `Content-Type` is the media type (`model/x3d+xml`, `application/json`, `text/turtle`, ...; anything unrecognised is stored as `application/octet-stream`)
Metadata answers are JSON with `Cache-Control: no-store`.
400 | id is not 64 hex characters; corrupt or truncated compressed stream, or bytes after the last gzip member or zstd frame that do not start another
